newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam urges quick return of Hong Kong boatpeople.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam urges quick return of Hong Kong boatpeople.

text.p: Vietnam called on Thursday for Hong Kong and the United Nations to quicken the return of boatpeople from detention camps before the British colony is handed back to China at midnight on June 30.

"Vietnam has urged the British/Hong Kong side and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) to accelerate efforts to repatriate to Vietnam all the refugees it had agreed to take back...," the official Vietnam News Agency said.

It referred to a March meeting between Vietnamese officials, the UNHCR and Hong Kong authorities at which Hanoi proposed April 15 as a target date for the roughly 2,500 detainees now cleared for repatriation.
However, a source who attended the meeting said Vietnam had already accepted that date was unrealistic.
"I don't know why they are putting the date up again," said the source, who declined to be identified. "Perhaps it's a question of tactics."
VNA said Vietnam had also proposed May 31 for completion of the Comprehensive Plan of Action (CPA). The CPA was introduced in 1989 at the height of the boatpeople exodus from Vietnam.

Under the plan, people who arrived in regional countries of first asylum were required to pass a screening test to establish their claims to refugee status. Those who failed were told they would have to return, or be returned, home.
The CPA was officially wrapped up in mid-1996, though UNHCR funding for Hong Kong camps has continued beyond that date.
The UNHCR's representative in Hanoi, Catherine Bertrand, said there were 3,800 still in Hong Kong camps at the end of March, of which between 1,000 and 1,200 were likely to return this month.

More than 1,000 people, many of them ethnic Chinese, have not yet been cleared by Vietnam for return. However, VNA said the Vietnamese had asked for access to the camps this month to establish the nationalities of those still uncleared.
How many will be left after the handover of Hong Kong remains to be seen, though one source said he expected the figure to be less than one thousand.
Vietnam has in the past been accused of dragging its feet on the return of the boatpeople.
But Bertrand said the VNA report underlined the desire of all parties to conclude the repatriation process.
"The signal is that everyone wants to finish the operation as soon as possible," she said. "What we all want is for the problem to be solved as soon as possible."
